newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Progress will prompt Israel to ease sanctions-Ross.
newsitem.headline: Progress will prompt Israel to ease sanctions-Ross.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross said on Wednesday he believed Israel would ease stringent sanctions imposed on the West Bank and Gaza Strip once security cooperation with the Palestinian Authority was restored.
"I think that as security cooperation goes forward I believe that in fact you'll see an easing of the measures," Ross told Cable News Network (CNN) in an interview in Jerusalem.

Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip and froze the transfer of crucial tax and customs revenue to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's administration after two suicide bombers killed 14 people in a Jerusalem market last month.

Ross flew to the area at the weekend to try to restore security coordination between Israel and the Palestinians. He told CNN he had made a "beginning" to resumed contacts with U.S. involvement and would now wait to assess the results.

As he was giving the interview, Israeli security forces blew up a suspicious package in the street outside the building. The scare, one of many false alarms in Jerusalem, was caused by someone leaving a bag unattended, witnesses said.
Israeli officials say Moslem bombers carried out the attack aided by an infrastructure of militants inside the areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under Arafat's control.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has accused Arafat of silently condoning activity of Moslem militants and demands a crackdown.

Arafat insists he is making a "100 percent effort" on security and accuses Israel of using the bombing as a pretext to weaken his legitimacy. He says security cooperation must be accompanied by political progress in peacemaking.
Ross, who has said repeatedly his mission since the weekend is to restore security cooperation, told CNN the political dimension must also be addressed.

"In this process we are going to have to address the needs of both sides, the concerns of both sides. There is no way to make progress if one is addresssing only one side's concerns. We know that. We have communicated that to both sides."
Ross was expected to return to Washington later on Wednesday.
